Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) of time series aims to teach models to identify consistent patterns across various temporal scenarios, disregarding domain-specific differences, which can maintain their predictive accuracy and effectively adapt to new domains.

Unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) of time series aims to teach models to identify consistent patterns across various temporal scenarios, disregarding domain-specific differences, which can maintain their predictive accuracy and effectively adapt to new domains.

To address this issue, we propose the \textbf{Lo}cal-\textbf{G}l\textbf{o}bal \textbf{R}epresentation \textbf{A}lignment framework (\abbr), which employs a two-branch encoder—comprising a multi-scale convolutional branch and a patching transformer branch.

To address this issue, we propose the \textbf{Lo}cal-\textbf{G}l\textbf{o}bal \textbf{R}epresentation \textbf{A}lignment framework (\abbr), which employs a two-branch encoder—comprising a multi-scale convolutional branch and a patching transformer branch.

A fusion module is then introduced to integrate these representations, enhancing domain-invariant feature alignment from multi-scale perspectives.

To achieve effective alignment, \abbr employs strategies like invariant feature learning on the source domain, utilizing triplet loss for fine alignment and dynamic time warping-based feature alignment.
